issues.title: Acquisition fee mismatch between OM and PPM
issues.expected_finding: The Offering Memorandum states a 2.0% acquisition fee, but the PPM fee schedule (the governing document) states 2.75%. On a $27,800,000 purchase price that is a $208,500 difference.

evidence.quote: Acquisition fee: 2.75% of purchase price, payable at closing

issues.title: Pro forma exit cap rate is tighter than the market study's prevailing cap rate
issues.note: The contradiction itself (5.0% vs. the 5.5-6.0% market range) is verifiable. Whether 5.0% is an unreasonable assumption to underwrite to is judgment_required.
issues.expected_finding: The pro forma applies a 5.0% exit cap rate, while the market study reports prevailing cap rates of 5.5-6.0% (midpoint 5.75%) for comparable stabilized value-add assets in the same submarket. Using the market midpoint instead of 5.0% would reduce the projected Year-5 exit value from $30,410,000 to roughly $26,443,000 on the same NOI.

evidence.quote: prevailing cap rates for stabilized value-add multifamily assets in the North Marrowdale submarket currently range from 5.5% to 6.0%, with a midpoint of approximately 5.75%

issues.title: Pro forma Year-1 occupancy assumption has no lease-up bridge from current in-place occupancy
issues.expected_finding: The rent roll shows current in-place physical occupancy of 87.8% (130/148 units). The pro forma assumes 94% stabilized occupancy starting in Year 1, with no explicit lease-up timeline, turnover downtime, or associated cost bridge shown between the two figures.

issues.title: Sponsor's "never lost investor capital" claim glosses over a return-of-capital-only exit
issues.expected_finding: The sponsor bio states Vantrel 'has never lost investor capital across its 11 realized exits.' The track record table shows the Brindlecrest Apartments exit (2016-2019) returned only investor capital with no profit distribution due to capex overruns. That statement is technically true but the framing implies a stronger track record than a break-even outcome represents. Whether this is meaningfully misleading is a judgment call, not a factual error.
